name: Tobiah
overview: Tobiah is a male biblical figure noted primarily for the uncertainty surrounding his Israelite heritage, as Scripture indicates he was unable to provide evidence of being from Israel. Beyond this unique attribute, there is little additional information about his tribe or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Tobiah means 'y-h-v-h is good,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that acknowledges the goodness of the Lord. This proper name, found in Ezra 2:60, was not given by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tobiah beyond the fact that he could not prove his Israelite descent. No other relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tobiah's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his uncertain identity within the community of Israel, highlighting the importance of lineage and heritage in the post-exilic period. His mention underscores the strict genealogical requirements for participation in the restoration of Israel, as recorded in Ezra 2:60. This serves as a reminder of God's covenantal promises to His people and the necessity of faithfulness to those covenants.
